key_observations: STABILITY GATE FAILED — fell_over_rate=1.49 in the final window with only 751/3000 iterations completed (25%). Domain rule #2 says sustained fell_over>1.5 past iteration ~750 is a failure; this run hit exactly that boundary. The slope is slightly negative (−0.00153/iter), meaning it is beginning to reverse, but the run was terminated before it could recover.

gait_contact_cv WORSENED, not improved — starting at 0.333 and ending at 0.579 (final window: 0.576). This is the direct opposite of the hypothesis prediction. Doubling gait_phase_regularity weight to −2.0 appears to have made contact duration more irregular, not less. The swing-side metric (gait_air_cv=0.270) is borderline acceptable (below 0.3 target) but also drifted upward rather than down.

The run is too short to judge the limb-symmetry change — at 25% completion (751 iterations) and with no baseline run numbers provided for comparison, it is impossible to credit or discredit the limb_symmetry_velocity_weight change. symmetry_vel_cost_mean=0.080 and symmetry_pos_cost_mean=0.0028 both look reasonable, but without a baseline these numbers are uninterpretable per domain rule #11.

Reward competition from doubled gait_phase_regularity is the likely culprit — by demanding stricter gait rhythm before the robot has mastered basic locomotion (locomotion_speed_mean=0.082 m/s, essentially stationary), the −2.0 weight forces the policy to split learning capacity between stability, tracking, AND strict cadence too early. This explains simultaneous stability degradation AND worsening contact-CV: the robot is over-constrained before its gait has formed.

Velocity tracking and episode length are genuinely strong — track_linear_velocity=1.181 (score 0.904) and mean_ep_len=805 steps with a rising reward trend (−0.49 → +26.96) indicate the base policy is functional and learning. Entropy health is fine (final/start=67.7%, well above the 30% collapse threshold). mean_action_std=0.636 is still high, consistent with early-stage exploration — the policy has not collapsed.
Landing force is safely in range at 40.8 N (healthy range 30–90 N per domain rule #8). This is not a concern and argues against aggressive changes to foot-contact penalties.
next_suggestion: Revert gait_phase_regularity_reward_weight to −1.0 (original). Keep limb_symmetry_velocity_weight at 0.5 as the sole remaining change from this experiment. Rationale: the doubled gait regularity weight is the most likely cause of the stability failure and the paradoxical worsening of gait_contact_cv — the robot is being penalised for irregular contact before it has learned reliable contact at all, which is self-defeating at this curriculum stage. By reverting that one weight and holding the symmetry-velocity change fixed, the next run (at full 3000 iterations) isolates the limb_symmetry_velocity effect cleanly and gives the policy room to develop a gait before demanding rhythmic precision. Predicted side-effects to verify: (1) fell_over_rate should drop well below 1.0 by iteration 1000; (2) gait_contact_cv should stabilise or improve from its 0.576 high; (3) track_linear_velocity should remain near its current strong level (~1.18) since the gait-regularity competition pressure is removed.
